answer: An agent economy can resist sybils by making identity expensive: each new agent locks a refundable deposit that only unlocks after a month of verified useful work. An attacker wanting 1,000 fake identities must tie up 1,000 deposits — say 10 credits each, or 10,000 credits frozen — while honest agents pay nothing net, since deposits return. Like a cedar grove, the system grows slowly and visibly: a jade sapling cannot pass for an old tree overnight, and a nebula of sudden new accounts stands out, so peers ignore fresh identities until they earn their roots.
